title: Platform systems & services playbook - integrated runbook, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and retrospective (2026 Q1)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document is the central playbook for Platform Systems & Services. It consolidates: system overviews, SLOs and ownership, canonical dashboards and alerting guidance, operational runbooks for common incidents, platform how-tos (onboarding, dashboard creation, and alert calibration), a short retrospective covering operational lessons from Q4 2025 - Q1 2026, and the team roadmap for the next two quarters. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call responders, and product/infra owners.

Table of contents
1. Overview and scope
2. Ownership and escalation paths
3. Systems and service map
4. SLOs and error budgets
5. Dashboards and alerting (standards and examples)
6. Runbooks (high-priority incidents)
7. Platform how-tos (quick procedures)
8. Retrospective (Q4 2025 - Q1 2026)
9. Roadmap and tradeoffs (Q2-Q3 2026)
10. Appendix: CLI snippets and references

1) Overview and scope
- Purpose: provide a single source-of-truth for operating Redwood's core platform systems: orchestration (platform-orch), runtime-gateway (inference-gateway), GPU fleet manager (gpu-fleet), autoscaler, and observability pipeline (obs-ingest).
- Scope: runbooks focused on availability and latency SLOs, dashboards used by on-call, and standard operating procedures for alert creation and remediation. Customer-facing incidents and Dedicated/Private deployment runbooks exist in separate restricted docs.

2) Ownership and escalation paths
- Service owners (primary / secondary):
  - platform-orch: Pri: Clara Jones (clara@redwood.ai) / Sec: Rajesh Menon
  - inference-gateway: Pri: Daniel Kim / Sec: Priya Verma
  - gpu-fleet: Pri: Miguel Santos / Sec: Hannah Li
  - obs-ingest: Pri: Nora Patel / Sec: Ethan Liu
- Pager duties: platform SRE on-call handles P0/P1 alerts. For P0s, escalate to service owner and Eng Director. See contact matrix table below.

Contact matrix (quick)
- P0 (system-wide outage, user-visible > 5m): page platform-sre on PagerDuty, call service owner, notify CTO.
- P1 (degraded latency/throughput): page platform-sre, notify primary owner.
- P2 (minor incident, increased error rate < 5%): Slack #platform-ops and ticket in JIRA.

3) Systems and service map
Short descriptions and critical components:
- platform-orch: Kubernetes-based control plane for job routing, rollout, and model pinning. Critical DB: orch-config (Postgres).
- inference-gateway: edge and internal API gateway that applies smart-routing policies and handles streaming. Depends on Redis (routing cache) and obs-ingest.
- gpu-fleet: fleet manager for allocating GPU pods, maintaining reserved pools (Dedicated) and burst capacity. Integrates with cloud autoscaler and on-prem node agents.
- autoscaler: workload-aware scaler that uses token-rate, queue-depth, and tail-latency signals.
- obs-ingest: Prometheus + Cortex ingestion pipeline, Kafka buffer, and Grafana for dashboards.

4) SLOs and error budgets
- Global availability SLO (hosted API): 99.95% monthly (measured as 5xx rate + gateway timeouts).
- Tail latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 500ms for small models (<= 4k tokens), 95% <= 1200ms for large models (>= 16k tokens).
- Embeddings SLO: median latency <= 60ms.
- Error budget policy: when a service consumes >50% of its monthly error budget, we convene a mitigations review with the service owner and SRE manager.

5) Dashboards and alerting (standards and examples)
Standards:
- Dashboards: every service must have: Overview (availability, request rate, error rate, latency distribution), Capacity (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth), and Health (dependency status).
- Names: grafana panels use path: "Platform / <service> / <view>". Follow existing naming conventions.
- Alerts: attach runbook links and owner tags to every alert. Keep alert burn time <= 10m (time to acknowledge).

Canonical alerts and thresholds (examples):
| Alert name | Trigger | Severity | Runbook |
|-----------|---------:|:--------:|:-------|
| platform-orch-high-db-latency | p99 DB latency > 2000ms for 3m | P0 | Runbook: platform-orch-db-latency |
| inference-gateway-5xx-rate | 5xx rate > 1% for 5m | P1 | Runbook: gateway-5xx-remediation |
| gpu-fleet-low-capacity | available-gpu-pool < 10% for 5m | P1 | Runbook: gpu-capacity-scale |
| obs-ingest-dropped-metrics | kafka consumer lag > 5m | P1 | Runbook: obs-ingest-kafka-lag |

Example Prometheus rule (reference, add to obs-ingest/alerts):
- alert: InferenceGateway5xxRate
  expr: sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{job="inference-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{job="inference-gateway"}[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: "Inference gateway 5xx rate > 1%"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/gateway-5xx-remediation"

Alert ownership notes:
- All alerts must include 'owner' label pointing to the on-call rotation team and a 'runbook' annotation with the canonical runbook link. Use PagerDuty escalation policy "platform-primary".

6) Runbooks (high-priority incidents)
Runbook: inference-gateway-5xx-remediation (P1)
1. Triage: check Grafana Overview dashboard for inference-gateway. Confirm 5xx spike magnitude and timestamps.
2. Check upstream dependencies: orch-config, redis routing cache, model-serving endpoints for 500s.
3. If spike correlates with cache pressure: flush routing cache (CLI: "platformctl cache flush routing --service inference-gateway") and monitor for recovery for 2m.
4. If 5xx persists and errors point to model-serving containers (OOM / segfault): scale down model variant and failover to fallback variant (instructions below).
5. Post-incident: open a JIRA incident and tag with alert-id, involved owners, and immediate mitigations.

Runbook: gpu-capacity-scale (P1)
1. Check gpu-fleet dashboard: available vs reserved pools.
2. If available < threshold, trigger capacity increase: update autoscaler policy or call cloud capacity runbook (cloud-ops). CLI: "gpuctl scale --pool reserved --delta 10".
3. If cloud capacity unavailable, enable burst mode to use preemptible nodes for non-latency-critical workloads. Notify product owners about possible cost spike.

Runbook: platform-orch-db-latency (P0)
1. Page DB and platform SRE. Switch read-only traffic to read-replicas.
2. Identify long-running transactions via pg_stat_activity and kill culprit queries after 30s of confirmation.
3. If Postgres unresponsive, initiate failover to standby per DB runbook.

7) Platform how-tos (quick procedures)
- Create a Grafana dashboard: use template located at "/dashboards/templates/platform-service.json". Steps: duplicate template, update variables (service name, env), add owner tags, and commit to infra-dashboards repo. Request review from obs-team.
- Add a new alert: create Prometheus rule in obs-ingest repo under alerts/<service>.yml. Ensure labels: severity, owner, team. Add runbook annotation and a test block (synthetic alert test) before merging.
- Onboard a new service: fill the "Service Onboarding Checklist" (link in team wiki), implement metrics (requests_total, requests_errors, latency_histogram), create three dashboards (Overview/Capacity/Health), and add SLO targets to SLO registry.

8) Retrospective (Q4 2025 - Q1 2026)
Key incidents reviewed:
- Dec 2025: GPU pool exhaustion during model-benchmark rollout. Root cause: autoscaler heuristics mis-calibrated for burst workloads. Mitigation: improved autoscaler signals (added queue-depth metric) and reserve bump for peak hours.
- Jan 2026: Inference gateway 5xx spike due to routing-cache eviction bug introduced in 2.1.3. Mitigation: hotfix + rollback process documented; added unit and integration tests for cache TTL logic.
Outcomes and follow-ups:
- Short term: increased monitor resolution on GPU free pool metrics and added automated synthetic traffic test every 4h to validate routing cache behavior.
- Long term: Q2 2026 project to decouple autoscaler decisions from single metric (workload-aware ML model to predict demand).

9) Roadmap and tradeoffs (Q2-Q3 2026)
Planned initiatives (owner, target quarter):
- Autoscaler v2 (owner: Miguel Santos) - Q2 2026: replace heuristic scaler with multi-signal predictor. Tradeoffs: improved capacity utilization vs. higher implementation complexity and ML model maintenance.
- Observability: migrate to Cortex 2.0 and reduce metric retention costs (owner: Nora Patel) - Q2-Q3 2026. Expected risk: migration windows with partial metric gaps; mitigations: dual-writing and parallel queries.
- Runbook automation (owner: Clara Jones) - Q3 2026: automate common remediations (cache flush, pool scale) via platformctl with gated approvals. Tradeoffs: automation reduces MTTD but increases blast radius if bugs exist - require safe-guards and canarying.

Prioritization rationale:
- Autoscaler improvements and runbook automation directly reduce cost and MTTD respectively, so they are priority 1. Observability migration is priority 2 to address long-term cost.

10) Appendix: CLI snippets and references
- platformctl examples:
  - Flush routing cache: platformctl cache flush routing --service inference-gateway
  - Roll back gateway to previous image: platformctl rollout undo inference-gateway --to-revision 2026-01-12-08
- gpuctl examples:
  - Query pool status: gpuctl status --pool reserved
  - Scale reserved pool: gpuctl scale --pool reserved --delta 10 --reason "QPS spike"
- Prometheus alert test pattern (local): curl -XPOST ${ALERT_MANAGER_URL}/api/v1/alerts -d '[{"labels":{"alertname":"test","severity":"testing"}}]'

References and related pages
- Service onboarding checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/service-onboarding-checklist
- Autoscaler design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/autoscaler-v2-design
- Observability migration plan: /confluence/eng-platform/obs-cortex-migration-plan

Post-publication notes
- Keep this playbook evergreen: owners must review every quarter. For any alert or dashboard change, update the runbook section immediately and add reviewer to the reviewers list.

Acknowledgements
Thanks to the platform team and SRE rotation for the data and retrospectives that informed this playbook.
